reasons: The rule is a 'missing'-kind insurance check, and Section 14.6 is a genuine, mutual insurance covenant (including product liability) running through clinical testing and commercialization, so the missing/insert trigger is not engaged and the deterministic check confirms an insurance obligation is present.

The rationale accurately reflects the quoted text: evidence of insurance on request, one-way advance notice from RevMed of cancellation/non-renewal/material change, self-insurance permitted only for Sanofi (our side), and an express statement that insurance does not cap Article XIV indemnification — all neutral or favourable to us, so no redline is warranted.

Shortfalls versus the preferred position (no CGL 1M/2M, no E&O or cyber towers, no one-year tail) are correctly recorded in the rationale rather than redlined; the walk-away scenario (no insurance for a data-processing or on-site vendor) is not engaged for a licensor/co-development counterparty, and the rule is low severity.
Consistent with the claimed compliant status, no redline text was changed and no counterparty comment was proposed, so there is no risk of over-flagging or an invalid edit.

Minor: describing a limits-free 'normal business practices' standard as sitting squarely 'at the fallback' (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is generous phrasing, but the rationale discloses the absence of stated limits, so the classification remains defensible and non-actionable.
